enforcement.allowlists.meaning: Named allow-lists by which the stack records intentional exceptions for specific checks; this rule needs the orphan-feature allow-list holding features intentionally listed by no wagon.

enforcement.convention_nodes.meaning: Where the stack's convention definitions live, how a check identifies them, and the authoring repository the followability check is gated to; the corpus is scanned whole (all definitions, not only changed ones).
bunValues: Convention nodes are YAML files identifiable by kind/location in the toolkit checkout; every existing node is in scope on every validation run, edited or not; the run is platform-gated to the toolkit source repo (consumer repos excluded).

enforcement.naming_exception_list.meaning: Where explicit, reviewable naming exceptions (brand or proper-noun slugs exempt from the verb-object rule) are listed; an unlisted exception is a violation.

enforcement.presets.meaning: For each kind of work (planning, building, instrumenting, coordinating), the preset of profiles to recommend: local profile names, conditional additions (documentation, web UI, runtime integration), the checks a preset's profile already bundles so that no later preset is proposed for them, the optional coordination profile's companion-tool condition, the legacy-to-successor one-for-one migration pairing, and the configuration key that holds the active profile list.
bunValues: planning=[planner]; building=[coder, tester, traceability, security]; instrumenting=[telemetry]; coordinating=[flow]; conditional additions: docs (planning, when the repository keeps documentation under docs/), htmx and design (building, web UI), interlocking (building, once trains have a runtime); coder already bundles the architecture, metrics, runtime, design and responsive detectors, so no later preset is proposed for them; flow only after the Flow companion is installed locally; legacy delivery/workflow -> flow one-for-one is not a loosening; the active list is the profiles: key of atdd-bun.yaml.

enforcement.profile_registries.meaning: For each profile, the location of its registry: a deterministic, profile-scoped projection of detector manifests, convention paths and direct relationship edges, to be read instead of the complete graph.
bunValues: architecture=conventions/_profiles/architecture.yaml, coder=conventions/_profiles/coder.yaml, design=conventions/_profiles/design.yaml, docs=conventions/_profiles/docs.yaml, htmx=conventions/_profiles/htmx.yaml, interlocking=conventions/_profiles/interlocking.yaml, metrics=conventions/_profiles/metrics.yaml, planner=conventions/_profiles/planner.yaml, runtime=conventions/_profiles/runtime.yaml, security=conventions/_profiles/security.yaml, telemetry=conventions/_profiles/telemetry.yaml, tester=conventions/_profiles/tester.yaml, topology=conventions/_profiles/topology.yaml, traceability=conventions/_profiles/traceability.yaml, flow=conventions/_profiles/flow.yaml

enforcement.schema_location.meaning: Where the enforcing package ships the schema that each recognized plan artifact kind must satisfy, and in which schema technology (e.g. JSON Schema in a shipped schemas directory).
bunValues: JSON Schema per kind, shipped in `planner-schemas/`

idiom.a11y_audit.meaning: The stack's automated accessibility audit harness: how a test invokes it and where the reported violations are exposed.
bunValues: import `AxeBuilder` from `@axe-core/playwright` (under any local name); `new AxeBuilder(...).analyze()` returns the result whose `violations` carries the findings.

idiom.acceptance_assertion_kinds.meaning: The exclusive allow-list of assertion kinds a `then` assertion may use in the stack's acceptance schema.
bunValues: status, body, headers, error, event_published, state_changed, metric

idiom.acceptance_precondition_fields.meaning: The precondition fields the stack's acceptance schema lists for an acceptance's `given` section (a listed vocabulary, not an exclusive allow-list).

idiom.acceptance_urn_derivation.meaning: The stack's construct that derives an acceptance URN from its inputs, with the exact input mapping.
bunValues: URNBuilder.acceptance(wagon slug, WMBT ID, harness code, sequence)

idiom.acceptance_when_shapes.meaning: The trigger form an acceptance's `when` must take for each harness kind the stack's acceptance schema defines.
bunValues: http → method/path; unit → target; event → topic; ws/e2e → interactions

idiom.action_route_map.meaning: The composition-root construct that maps each entrypoint action to a route (direct train, grouping, or journey form).
bunValues: JOURNEY_MAP in server.ts; additive forms: "train:<subject>:<slug>", { interlockingId, path }, { journeyId, path }

idiom.adhoc_print_calls.meaning: The stack's concrete ad-hoc print or logging calls (no level, timestamp or correlation) that application source must not use for output.
bunValues: console.log, console.info, console.warn, console.error, console.debug, console.trace, console.dir

idiom.appendix_types.meaning: The appendix types a stack recognizes; the {type} segment of an appendix filename may take only these values.
bunValues: the six recognized appendix types enumerated by planner.appendix.types (bun.json examples: mockup, diagram, spreadsheet)

idiom.archival_status_marker.meaning: The stack's concrete construct with which an archived document records its archival (what the core's 'archival status marker' instantiates to).

idiom.authorization_check.meaning: How a handler serving a mutating endpoint decides authorization, and the client error it answers with on failure.

idiom.bare_http_calls.meaning: The stack's concrete bare outbound-HTTP call forms — direct calls to the platform's raw HTTP primitive or to an unmediated HTTP-client library — whose use in a consumer-role file this rule forbids; checked over masked source.
bunValues: A bare `fetch(` or `axios(` call, detected by scanning masked source (strings/comments masked out)

idiom.barrel_module.meaning: How the stack identifies a barrel — a module that only re-exports other modules; a barrel re-export is not consumption.

idiom.bounded_unit.meaning: The stack's concrete construct for a bounded slice of the product inside one composition domain; behavior internal to one bounded unit does not cross a composition-domain boundary.

idiom.breakpoint_matching.meaning: How a width in a condition is matched to a declared breakpoint: the tolerance below a breakpoint and unit conversion applied before matching.
bunValues: A `max-width` X matches breakpoint B when X == B or B-1 <= X < B (within 1px below, e.g. `767px`, `767.98px` for 768); `em`/`rem` convert to px at 16px before matching

idiom.breakpoints.meaning: Where the stack configures the widths at which responsive conditions (media queries) may switch.

idiom.breakpoints_declaration.meaning: Where the stack declares the responsive breakpoints that width conditions may use (config file and entry, with the default set).

idiom.cargo_calls.meaning: The stack's concrete construct by which a module moves artifacts through Cargo (get/put or equivalent), used to recognise Cargo-moving modules structurally rather than by filename, and to find where declared artifact names must appear.
bunValues: cargo.get(name) / cargo.put(name, value) method calls on the Cargo passed to the wagon (e.g. in runWagon(step, cargo): const basket = cargo.get(CONSUMES); cargo.put(PRODUCES, { confirmed: true, basket });)

idiom.cli_interface_output.meaning: How a CLI entry point writes user-facing interface output directly to the standard output and error streams (interface output, not a log).

idiom.collaborator_construction.meaning: The stack's construct for constructing a collaborator instance, whose use must be confined to a composition root.

idiom.collaborator_naming.meaning: Name patterns that mark a type as a collaborator (repository, client, gateway, factory, provider and the like) whose wiring belongs in a composition root.
bunValues: class names ending in Repository, Client, Service, Adapter, Gateway, Store, Provider, Factory

idiom.collaborator_substitution.meaning: The stack's test constructs that replace or intercept a production collaborator (module mocks, spies, patching) — the concrete referent of the neutral term 'substitute a production collaborator'.
bunValues: mock.module, spyOn, jest.mock/spyOn, vi.mock/spyOn — replacing a production collaborator.

idiom.collection_contract.meaning: The stack's concrete construct for a collection contract (a plural aspect with a concrete collection) and how it references its singular contract, including the relative reference layout.
bunValues: array schema {type: array, items: $ref ../singular} — a JSON Schema of type array whose items $ref the singular aspect's schema one directory up (../<singular>.schema.json)

idiom.color_value_contexts.meaning: The concrete contexts in a UI artifact where a color value can be written and is read by the check.
bunValues: CSS declarations, `style` attributes, `<style>` blocks, JSX `style={{…}}` objects, `fill`/`stroke`/`bgcolor` attributes in .tsx, .jsx, .html, .htm, .css; plus inline `style="…"` attributes and `<style>` text in HTML a .ts/.mts file renders from string/template/tagged-template literals

idiom.comment_line_kinds.meaning: The comment-line forms the stack's source syntax admits (line-comment marker, block-comment delimiters, continuation lines inside a block comment), which a comment-ratio count uses as its numerator.
bunValues: line comments, block comments, and continuation lines beginning `*` inside a block comment

idiom.complexity_measure.meaning: How cyclomatic complexity is measured in the stack's syntax: which constructs count as decision points (control-flow branch forms, short-circuit and nullish operators, conditional expressions).
bunValues: complexity = 1 + each decision point. Decision points: if / else if / for / while / do / catch / case keywords, each && / || / ?? operator, each ternary.

idiom.component_event_props.meaning: Event-binding syntax of a different mechanism (component or template props rather than markup attributes) that resembles an inline handler and is exempt from inline-handler rules.
bunValues: React/JSX camelCase props (`onClick={…}`, `onSubmit={…}`); only these props are exempt, not JSX files as such

idiom.component_export.meaning: How the stack identifies an exported design-system component among a file's exports.
bunValues: a capitalized export (lowercase exports are non-component helpers or values)

idiom.component_type_catalog.meaning: The stack's canonical component type catalog: every component type keyed by side and layer, each with per-language file-name suffix(es), description and complexity weight; side.layer.type is the lookup key and supplies the side/layer values of component URNs; an entry with no suffix for a language makes the type unavailable there.
bunValues: sharedNodes[context.component-type-catalog] in bun.json: sides backend|frontend; layers presentation, application, domain, integration; backend languages python|typescript, frontend languages dart|typescript; every entry 'type — suffix(es) per language — description — weight'; lookup key side.layer.type (full entry list in that node)

idiom.component_type_weights.meaning: Per product side x layer x granular component type -> weight, verbatim. The component types are the stack's coder-convention types; every weight instantiates the universal 0-3 complexity scale. The core's footprint formula reads this table.
bunValues:
backend.presentation: controllers 1, routes 0, serializers 0.5, validators 0.5, middleware 1, guards 1, views 1.
backend.application: use_cases 2, handlers 1, ports 0, dtos 0, policies 1, workflows 2.
backend.domain: entities 1, value_objects 0.5, aggregates 2, services 1, specifications 0.5, events 0, exceptions 0.
backend.integration: repositories 2, clients 1, caches 0.5, engines 3, formatters 1, notifiers 1, queues 2, stores 1, mappers 0.5, schedulers 2, monitors 1.
frontend.presentation: views 1, components 0.5, containers 1, controllers 2, routes 0, layouts 1, styles 0, animations 0.5, forms 1, hooks 0.5, directives 0.5, filters 0.5.
frontend.application: use_cases 2, ports 0, policies 1, dtos 0.
frontend.domain: entities 1, value_objects 0.5, services 1, specifications 0.5, exceptions 0.
frontend.integration: repositories 2, clients 1, stores 1, serializers 0.5, mappers 0.5, interceptors 1, caches 0.5, synchronizers 2, monitors 1, validators 0.5, workers 2, connectors 1.

idiom.composition_domain.meaning: The stack's concrete construct for a runtime composition domain; runtime behavior crossing the boundary between two composition domains needs new declared runtime semantics.

idiom.consume_producer_reference.meaning: The syntax by which a consume entry in a plan artifact (wagon manifest) names the wagon that produces the consumed artifact.

idiom.contract_external_marker.meaning: The marker on a produced contract that declares it consumed outside the plan graph (exempts the unconsumed invariant only).

idiom.contract_identity_field.meaning: The schema-format construct by which a contract schema declares its identity — the stack-neutral core's 'identity field'.

idiom.contract_path_mapping.meaning: The stack's construct for deriving a produced artifact's contract-file path from the artifact identity: identity grammar and boundary characters, the contract root directory, the contract-file suffix and leaf naming, and any short-identity edge case.
bunValues: Split the identity on ':' and '.'. The segments are directories under contracts/, and the leaf is the .schema.json file; a two-segment identity's leaf name also appears as the final directory (match:config -> contracts/match/config/config.schema.json).

idiom.contract_reference.meaning: The syntax by which a plan artifact's produce/consume entry references a contract: a contract field that holds a contract URN (its prefix is stripped to obtain the registered identity) or null.
bunValues: contract: URN / contract: null; strip the 'contract:' URN prefix before lookup

idiom.convention_node_id_field.meaning: The field of a convention-node artifact that carries the node's rule id — the identifier that relationship-graph edges reference.

idiom.convention_operative_fields.meaning: How a convention definition's fields divide into operative prose (strings a reader is expected to act on) versus provenance records and illustrative example blocks — only operative prose makes a promise.
bunValues: Operative: `fix_hint`, `operational_guidance`, `normative_text`, `statement`, term `text`, `notes`, `description`. Excluded: provenance (`source.legacy_path` + `legacy_sha`) and `examples`/`values` blocks.

idiom.coverage_exceptions.meaning: How the stack declares coverage exceptions: the config location and the per-gap allow-list keys, each with its documented use case.
bunValues: coverage.exceptions.wagons_not_in_train (utility/shared/under-development wagons); coverage.exceptions.features_orphaned (deprecated/experimental features); coverage.exceptions.wmbts_without_acceptance (draft/placeholder WMBTs), in .atdd/config*

idiom.coverage_status_exemption.meaning: The plan-artifact status value that marks genuinely unfinished (in-progress) work.

idiom.decision_declaration.meaning: The construct by which a decision record declares the architectural decision it records.

idiom.decision_record_declaration.meaning: How a decision record declares its identity and the node it decides — the edge the registry entries are keyed by and derived from.
bunValues: :adr-id: and :decides: attributes in each ADR file (one registry line per ADR keyed by :adr-id:)

idiom.decision_record_header.meaning: The required record-header attributes of every decision record (record metadata: identifier, status, date), besides the decision declaration.

idiom.declaration_load.meaning: The constructs by which a module in this stack reads and parses a plan-declaration file, so a check can recognize that the runtime loads the declaration.

idiom.declarative_behaviour_attributes.meaning: The markup framework's declarative constructs for declaring element behaviour (element-scoped behaviour and request triggering) that participate in its content-replacement lifecycle.
bunValues: `hx-on` for element-scoped behaviour, `hx-trigger` for the request itself; both survive swaps because htmx re-processes new content

idiom.declarative_token_form.meaning: The stack's declarative token-authoring file form: token files of this form are values by construction and are never scanned by value-only checks.

idiom.declared_train_sequence.meaning: How the declared wagon-step sequence of a train is expressed in the runtime/plan schema, which the journey runner must not loop over as an executor.

idiom.decomposition_reasoning_kinds.meaning: Decomposition candidate kinds that are real candidates the operator decides on but that author no artifact: a keep records a decision only (the reasoning granularities).

idiom.definition_anchor_id.meaning: The concrete construct by which a definition-anchor node is identified in the convention graph: the expected node id scheme per core domain artifact.

idiom.direct_train_execution.meaning: The stack's call that executes a train's steps directly, outside the TrainRunner.

idiom.doc_id_declaration.meaning: How an authored documentation document declares its own identifier; the declared-id set is read from these declarations.

idiom.doc_identity_attributes.meaning: How a documentation artifact declares its identity id and currency status in its header: the attribute names, their syntax, and the header position.
bunValues: :doc-id: and :status: AsciiDoc header attributes above the first section

idiom.doc_lifecycle.meaning: How the stack marks a document current vs superseded, and the construct by which a replacement declares succession of the archived document.

idiom.doc_relationship_attribute.meaning: The syntax by which an authored documentation document declares a relationship to another document by its declared id.

idiom.doc_relationship_attributes.meaning: The markup syntax by which an authored document declares its document identifier and references other documents by identifier — the relationship attributes the documentation-graph resolver resolves.

idiom.doc_status_marker.meaning: How a document declares its status (current vs historical/archived) in the stack's documentation markup format.

idiom.dto_declaration.meaning: How the stack declares and recognizes a DTO, the data shape crossing a boundary: the declaring construct and its naming pattern.
bunValues: a `type` or `interface` declaration whose name ends in `DTO`

idiom.dto_naming.meaning: Name patterns by which a type is recognized as a DTO (a boundary shape).

idiom.dto_purity.meaning: What pure immutable data means for a DTO in the stack: which member kinds count as behavior, and how field immutability is expressed.
bunValues: no method members; every field declared `readonly`

idiom.emission_assertion.meaning: The stack's assertion idioms that count as an emission assertion (spy/mock call matchers on the emitter, or expectations on emit-style methods).
bunValues: toHaveBeenCalled / toHaveBeenCalledWith / toHaveBeenCalledTimes on the emitter, or an expectation on .emit / .emitted / .capture / .track / .record

idiom.emission_assertions.meaning: The stack's test-assertion constructs that count as asserting on the emission via the captured sink.

idiom.endpoint_declarations.meaning: The declarative markup constructs (hypermedia verb attributes) whose occurrence in markup declares an endpoint; an endpoint-coverage rule enumerates every occurrence as part of the route space.

idiom.env_access.meaning: How code reads a configuration or credential value from the environment at the edge.

idiom.environment_mutation.meaning: The stack's concrete idiom for mutating the shared process environment, which the core forbids in test code and the check flags.

idiom.error_response_payload.meaning: How the stack constructs a response carrying an error status, and how a structured, serialized payload is returned as that response's body — the concrete referents of a core's 'error response (a response with a 4xx/5xx status)' and 'structured payload with an error code'. Stack data only; a rule's detection patterns and worked examples stay with the rule's realization.
bunValues: A response is the web-standard `Response` object: `new Response(<body>, { status })` returns a raw body, `Response.json(<payload>, { status })` serializes a structured payload as the response body.

idiom.external_actor.meaning: The syntax by which a plan artifact names an external actor (as opposed to a typed reference to a declared artifact).

idiom.feature_kind_declaration.meaning: The stack's concrete construct by which a feature plan artifact declares its kind (the neutral core's 'feature marked feedback-loop'), and on which a suppression marker can be placed.
bunValues: a `kind:` field on the feature YAML, e.g. `kind: feedback-loop`

idiom.feature_kind_line.meaning: The line (or construct) in a feature plan artifact where its kind is declared; inline rule suppressions attach to it.
bunValues: the `kind:` line of the planner feature file, e.g. `kind: feedback-loop`

idiom.fenced_example_block.meaning: The markup construct that fences literal/example blocks whose content illustrates shape and lists nothing.

idiom.file_read_tool.meaning: The tool the agent uses to read a referenced file path or URL (multimodal where applicable); transcript calls of this tool are the compliance evidence for read-before-use rules.
bunValues: the Read tool — the planner reads the referenced appendix path/URL by invoking the Read tool, and the compliance evidence is a Read tool call in the transcript

idiom.forbidden_runner_substitutions.meaning: The stack's test-double idioms that count as a forbidden substitution when aimed at a production runner or its route-resolution/execution behavior, including mock classes and hand-built resolvers standing in for the route-resolution runner; a migrating-framework spy idiom counts only when it replaces runner behavior.
bunValues: MockInterlockingRunner/MockTrainRunner; mock.module(...) replacing a runner module; spyOn(...)/mock(...)/mock.restore(...) aimed at a runner (bun:test); vi.mock(...)/jest.mock(...) around a runner module; vi.spyOn(...)/jest.spyOn(...) replacing runner behavior (resolveTrain/execute); a locally defined resolveTrain function or *Resolver class standing in for InterlockingRunner

idiom.forbidden_server_constructions.meaning: Construction expressions of compatibility/foreign HTTP servers that must not be constructed in non-test application source.
bunValues: express(), fastify(, new Koa(, http.createServer(, https.createServer(, bare createServer(

idiom.generated_region.meaning: How a machine-maintained generated region is delimited (and the name of the registry's region), so that only that span is read as a generated listing.
bunValues: `// BEGIN GENERATED: <name>` ... `// END GENERATED: <name>`, a span a generator rewrites in place; the registry's region is named `adr-register`

idiom.generated_region_marker.meaning: The marker pair a generator writes around its own output, delimiting the machine-maintained region that is regenerated in place and compared by checks.
bunValues: // BEGIN GENERATED: adr-register and // END GENERATED: adr-register

idiom.guard_grammar.meaning: The stack's concrete declarative grammar of routing-guard expressions in plan artifacts: allowed input kinds, allowed operators, and the presence-test call form. Anything outside the grammar is an invalid token.
bunValues: Inputs: action/request inputs, an explicit state snapshot, and a completed TrainResult only at declared route boundaries. Operators: == != < <= > >= and or not exists(field) in.

idiom.harness_codes.meaning: The stack's authoritative harness vocabulary: the codes naming the test layers that can exercise an acceptance criterion (the neutral concept 'harness type' that acceptance criteria declare). The profile value identifies the vocabulary and/or its complete membership; codes quoted in rules are illustrative examples.
bunValues: the authoritative harness vocabulary (illustrative member codes cited: UNIT, INTEGRATION, HTTP, E2E, SMOKE; complete membership not enumerated in bun.json)

idiom.harness_templates.meaning: The stack's harness template catalog for acceptance criteria: the harness kinds and, for each kind, the layers it typically exercises and its given/when/then scaffold, whose values are placeholders meant to be replaced with a criterion's real values.

idiom.human_participant.meaning: How a plan artifact's train declaration marks that a human takes part in the train; rules that gate on 'human-facing' journeys read this construct.
bunValues: a train declaration under plan/ listing a `user:` participant

idiom.hypermedia_markup_marker.meaning: How a file is recognized as hypermedia-driven markup: the declarative attribute family of the stack's markup framework; files without it are outside a self-scoping rule's scope.
bunValues: the file contains at least one `hx-` attribute

idiom.id_reaching_assertions.meaning: The stack's test-assertion forms that count as asserting a specific element id (the id-reaching forms this rule accepts).
bunValues: an `id=` inside an expected string, a `getElementById` call, a `querySelector('#…')`, or a `toHaveAttribute('id'…`)

idiom.inband_swap_construct.meaning: The declarative markup construct whose response swaps into the requesting element's declared target (a selector) rather than an id — the out-of-scope sibling of the out-of-band swap.
bunValues: hx-swap — swaps into hx-target, a selector, not an id

idiom.inline_event_handler_form.meaning: The exact form of the inline host event-handler attribute in markup that a rule forbids, including the case rule used to match it.
bunValues: a lowercase `on<event>="…"` attribute (onclick, onsubmit, onchange, …) carrying JavaScript in markup; matching is deliberately lowercase-only

idiom.integration_branch.meaning: How a named integration coordinator's linked integration branch (and worktree) is named, from which its drivers derive their governed base.

idiom.interactive_controls.meaning: The stack's raw interactive control constructs that application markup must render through design-system primitives.
bunValues: a lowercase `<button`, `<input`, `<select`, or `<textarea` element written in app code — in JSX, or in the body of a string/template/tagged-template literal in a `.ts`/`.mts` file — followed by whitespace, `>`, or `/`

idiom.interlocking_route.meaning: How a journey-map value that is a guarded interlocking route is distinguished from a direct train reference.
bunValues: a JOURNEY_MAP value that is an {interlockingId, path} route object (interlocking route), vs a direct trainId string (direct train)

idiom.interlocking_runner.meaning: The stack's construct and local name for the interlocking runner (local route selection), including its routing entry methods.

idiom.interlocking_runners.meaning: The stack's concrete symbols, entry points and full invocation shape for the two production interlocking runners of the call model — the route-resolution runner (constructed over the interlocking plan artifact, invoked with an action and inputs, resolving the guarded route to exactly one selected train) and the train-execution runner (which receives that selected train and executes it through the real runtime path) — including the selected-train handoff between the two runners.
bunValues: InterlockingRunner and TrainRunner; call model InterlockingRunner.resolveTrain -> TrainRunner.execute; construct new InterlockingRunner(interlockingYamlPath) and call .resolveTrain(action, inputs), which resolves the guarded route to exactly one trainId; pass that trainId to the production TrainRunner and execute the selected train through the real runtime path

idiom.internal_import.meaning: Which import specifier forms resolve a module reference to a target inside a tree of the project graph (e.g. relative specifiers and path aliases bound to a tree), so that an import counts as targeting that tree.
bunValues: a relative path into the design directory, or an aliased specifier whose alias names the design directory

idiom.internal_reference.meaning: The stack's concrete markup constructs for an internal cross-reference: how one document in the documentation corpus references another document or an anchor within it.

idiom.journey_entry_binding.meaning: How the stack binds each declared start-surface action to the journey entry (the concrete binding target and shape).
bunValues: binds the declared Station Master actions to {journeyId, path}

idiom.journey_executor.meaning: The stack's runtime component that may execute a journey, deliberately kept separate from the semantic journey definition.

idiom.journey_map.meaning: The composition root's action-to-route mapping construct (the journey map) itself; its placement is given by the existing roles.composition_root.path key.

idiom.journey_registry.meaning: The construct by which the stack's boundary surface declares its admitted journey space (the route registry); the declaring surface is located by this declaration's content, never by file name.
bunValues: a module-level declaration named JOURNEY_MAP; the module carrying it (the Station Master) is found by the JOURNEY_MAP it DECLARES, never by filename

idiom.journey_runner.meaning: The stack's construct and local name for the journey runner, the continuation-control layer that traverses declared journey topology between interlockings.
bunValues: JourneyRunner; Station Master -> JourneyRunner(journeyPath) -> InterlockingRunner -> TrainRunner

idiom.journey_start_surface.meaning: The stack's concrete name for the consumer-facing start surface whose actions start an exposed journey.

idiom.launch_surface.meaning: The product's concrete launch/entry surfaces that count as the real production entry point a launch-path test must drive — the surfaces exercising real command construction and the real launch path — as opposed to synthetic stand-ins.
bunValues: atdd spawn, atdd coach, and the rendered launch prompt — the surfaces that exercise real adapter command construction and the cmux-native launch path

idiom.length_unit_base.meaning: How relative length units in styling declarations are converted to absolute units for comparison.

idiom.logger_receivers.meaning: Receiver names that count as a logger in this stack, defining the scope of logging rules.

idiom.logging_context_shape.meaning: How a logger call carries its structured context: which argument position and what shape the context takes.
bunValues: the second argument carrying the fields a line will be searched by; a JS logger takes an object where a Python one takes `extra=` or kwargs

idiom.markup_id_binding.meaning: The forms in which a markup element carries its own id — literal attribute value and/or dynamic expression binding — and that an expression binding counts as present with resolution unchecked.
bunValues: literal id="…" on the element's own opening tag, or a JSX expression id={…}

idiom.markup_interpolation.meaning: The stack's construct for building markup with interpolated values — the interpolated string a markup-escape check scans for bare value interpolations.

idiom.name_token_separators.meaning: The exact characters on which a file's base name is split into tokens for name-token identification (base-name tokens only, never directory names or arbitrary substrings).
bunValues: split on `.`, `-`, `_` only; matched against tokens of the file's basename, never against directory names or arbitrary substrings

idiom.naming_exception_list.meaning: Where naming-rule exceptions (e.g. brand or proper-noun slugs) must be explicitly listed; anything unlisted is a violation.

idiom.naming_verb_lexicon.meaning: Where the stack declares the verb-selection lexicon: the allowed leading verbs for verb-object names.

idiom.native_server_construct.meaning: The runtime's native HTTP server construct that the application server must be built on.

idiom.observable_channels.meaning: The stack's operator-observable channels (e.g. transport response status/body, rendered markup, process output streams, exit code, persisted state) on which a SMOKE assertion may witness behaviour, and which its convention check recognizes.
bunValues: an HTTP response status or body, rendered markup, stdout/stderr, an exit code, or persisted state; the fix hint also admits other observable channels

idiom.oob_swap_construct.meaning: The declarative markup construct that marks an element for an out-of-band swap into the document; test bodies mention it in any form when an out-of-band swap is involved.

idiom.overflow_measure.meaning: The measurement construct a responsive browser test must use to detect horizontal overflow of the rendered page, including the derived values that count as the same measurement.
bunValues: `scrollWidth`, used directly or through a variable measured from it

idiom.phase_declaration.meaning: How a test file declares its test Phase (UNIT, SMOKE, ...) so a phase observer can read activation from the file's own declaration, never from a filename or location convention.
bunValues: The file's declared Phase, parsed by the detector's phase observer; no filename convention is assumed.

layout.model_portfolio.meaning: Where the coordination desk's model-portfolio record (launchable model candidates ordered strongest to weakest) lives.
bunValues: the Desk's models.yaml (**/models.yaml), ordered strongest to weakest

layout.orchestrator_dir.meaning: Location pattern of one theme orchestrator file (the artifact that implements a theme's trains), with a {theme} placeholder identifying the theme the file is responsible for.

layout.plan_metadata_file.meaning: Path of the planning protocol's plan-metadata file under the plan root, when the protocol defines one; rules that exclude this mechanism bind to exactly this designated file.

layout.plan_schema.meaning: Path of the schema that defines the plan artifact's format and owns the enums (e.g. dimension, direction) that derived tables must be total over.

layout.render_output.meaning: The tree the reference renderer writes its output to: generated output, never a render input.

layout.session_machine.meaning: Where the plan session machine's implementation files (session state, lock, author pass) live, relative to the source root.

layout.subject_registry.meaning: Path of the plan's subject registry: the single file in which every subject must be registered (unique-by-subject) before any train is typed under it, and against which naming and uniqueness are checked.

layout.telemetry_item.meaning: Path pattern of one tracking-plan item under the telemetry registry root, carrying the theme/artifact segments, the kind.plane[.measure] file-name grammar and the item file suffix.
bunValues: a JSON registry entry under telemetry/<theme>/<artifact>/ whose id is the referenced URN

layout.telemetry_manifest_input.meaning: The file set from which the generated telemetry manifest is built.

layout.telemetry_signal_dir.meaning: Directory of one telemetry URN's signal files, derived by splitting the URN into path segments.

layout.telemetry_signal_tree.meaning: Root glob of the telemetry signal tree; any file under it is an in-scope activation signal by location, independent of file-kind recognition.

layout.theme_registry.meaning: Path of the repository-owned theme registry (the canonical, repository-declared source of theme names), typically under the plan root.

layout.train_document_sidecars.meaning: Names or globs inside the per-train document tree that are registry sidecars (supporting artifacts of the registry), not per-train documents; excluded from the orphan enumeration only.
bunValues: underscore-prefixed names under plan/_trains: _aliases.yaml and the _interlockings/ subtree

layout.train_registry.meaning: Path of the registry index file that enumerates every train of the plan tree (with its grouping), relative to the repository root.

layout.trains_dir.meaning: Directory of the runtime trains layer (journey runner, interlocking runner, train runner) under the source root, where the journey runner must be shipped and scanned.

layout.wagon_entry.meaning: The entry module of one wagon — the module exposing the wagon's steps, whose import by interlocking code is the flagged pattern.

layout.wagon_module.meaning: Path pattern of one wagon's entry module — the module that speaks for the wagon — relative to the source root; the companion wagon-import scan targets these modules.

roles.dispatcher.name.meaning: The stack's local name for the dispatcher: the component that routes produced-artifact divergence to trains (an extension of the roles.<role>.name parametric family with a 'dispatcher' role param).

roles.harness_layers.meaning: The typical-layer catalog: for each harness, the layer roles it typically exercises; a harness with no entry has no typical layer.
bunValues: unit [domain, application]; http [integration, application]; event [application, integration]; ws [integration]; e2e [presentation]; a11y [presentation]; visual [presentation]; metric [application, integration]; job [application]; db [integration]; sec [application, integration]; load [integration]; script [application]; widget [presentation]; golden [presentation, application]; bloc [application]; integration [integration]; rls [integration]; edge_function [integration]; realtime [integration]; storage [integration]; smoke: no entry

roles.layer_profiles.meaning: Per-layer typical responsibilities (typical operations/methods, consumes, produces) that guide layer choice and layer-consistency review.
bunValues: presentation: typical methods render/handleInput/updateDisplay, consumes user interactions & display updates, produces ui events & user actions; application: typical methods execute/coordinate/validate, consumes commands & queries, produces events & responses; domain: typical methods process/calculate/applyRules, consumes domain events, produces domain events & state changes; integration: typical methods fetch/save/publish, consumes external events, produces external calls & persistence operations; assembly: no profile in source.

roles.layers.count.meaning: The number of dependency-ordered layer roles in the stack's layered structure, for guidance that refers to the structure by count.

roles.layers_per_side.meaning: The layer roles in which each side's components live: which layers frontend-side and backend-side components occupy, and what shared components count as.
bunValues: frontend -> presentation, application; backend -> application, domain, integration; shared -> cross-cutting concerns

roles.plan_artifact.granularity_ladder.meaning: The ordered kinds of plan artifact a decomposition must descend, from the coarsest slice kind to the terminal acceptance rung; defines which rungs are dangling when a decomposition skips levels.

roles.plan_artifact.levels.meaning: The stack's plan-decomposition levels with their local names: which local kind is the coarse plan artifact (the bounded product slice carrying description and scope) and which is the fine-grained plan item (carrying when/must/then statements, scenarios, steps and reproduce steps).
bunValues: coarse plan artifact -> wagon; fine-grained plan item -> WMBT

roles.plan_artifact.unit_name.meaning: What the stack calls the plan's decomposition unit — the bounded slice of the product that the plan defines — whose description is carried by the plan schema's existing description field.

roles.runtime.path.meaning: Where the modules forming the plan-executing runtime live (a path segment or glob); they are checked as one runtime surface, not per module.

roles.structural_names.meaning: The stack's filenames that name a structural role rather than a component (assembly, wiring, layout, entrypoint); exempt from component-identity checks such as the URN name-segment match.
bunValues: composition, wagon, entrypoint, http, index, schema, router, routes, server, layout, partial, fragment, middleware

roots.conventions.meaning: Tree or file where the stack's convention documents live; where train implementation patterns are documented.

roots.coordination.meaning: Root of the separate workflow coordination repository holding the durable coordination records; the workflow-profile observer and coordination-record file kinds resolve against it. Record-kind layout and file-name patterns live in separate keys (layout.coordination_records, suffix.coordination_record, layout.model_portfolio).
bunValues: the separate workflow root holding work/ and threads/

roots.design.meaning: Root of the repository's design system (where primitives live); application code outside it must compose its primitives, and a repository without it is not judged.
bunValues: a directory named `design`, `design_system`, or `design-system` (globs **/design/**, **/design_system/**, **/design-system/**); the first directory beneath it names the layer: `tokens` or `foundations`, `primitives`, `components`, `templates`

roots.design_system.meaning: Globs or directories under which the repository's shared design system (design root) lives; used for the repository-level existence precondition, for excluding design-system files themselves from candidacy, and for resolving which imports are design-system imports.

roots.docs.meaning: The top-level tree of the repository in which documentation artifacts live.

roots.docs_generated.meaning: Generated documentation output beneath roots.docs: build output that is a consequence of authored changes and is never required to be declared.

roots.telemetry.meaning: Root of the telemetry tracking-plan registry: the versioned source of truth for planned observations; a configured root replaces the default and does not add to it.
bunValues: `telemetry/` by default, configurable as topology.telemetry_root in atdd-bun.yaml

roots.theme_taxonomy.meaning: The file that declares the repository-defined theme taxonomy used to classify plan trains.

suffix.a11y_test.meaning: Name patterns that identify an accessibility spec among the stack's test files: an accessibility name token bounded in the file's base name (extends the file_kind param with a11y_test).

suffix.agent_instruction.meaning: Name patterns of the agent-instruction file kind: the files that carry managed projection blocks of the collaboration policy.

suffix.appendix_pattern.meaning: The filename pattern that identifies a file as an appendix (supplementary material describing a plan-structure artifact) and embeds the identifier of the artifact it describes.
bunValues: {artifact}_{type}_{slug}.ext (e.g. E023_mockup_payment-error.png); the artifact prefix in the filename should match the artifact that owns the appendices/ directory

suffix.appendix_types.meaning: The recognized appendix types of the stack's planner and, for each type, the file extensions allowed for appendix files of that type.
bunValues: mockup: PNG, JPG, JPEG, SVG, GIF; spreadsheet: XLSX, CSV, TSV; document: PDF, DOCX, MD, TXT; diagram: PNG, SVG, MERMAID, DRAWIO; audio: MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG; video: MP4, MOV, WEBM, AVI

suffix.barrel.meaning: Name patterns that identify the stack's barrel files (re-export-only entry files), so a rule can state its own policy over this file kind.

suffix.contract.meaning: File-name pattern of a contract document (the file kind a logical artifact name resolves to).

suffix.contract_schema.meaning: Suffix or name patterns that identify an interface contract schema file.

suffix.convention_node.meaning: Name pattern(s) that identify a convention-node artifact: a convention definition carrying a rule id, which is a node of the relationship graph.

suffix.coordination_record.meaning: File-name pattern of the durable coordination record kinds; the activation globs for record files resolve through this key.
bunValues: handover.yaml — the seat's one durable handover record (task/seat/checkpoint/thread records are YAML under work/ and threads/)

suffix.declaration_file.meaning: Name patterns that identify the stack's declaration-only files (ambient/declaration type files with no executable code), so a rule can state its own policy over this file kind.

suffix.documentation.meaning: Suffixes or name patterns that identify a documentation artifact (the file kind would extend the file_kind params with `documentation`).

suffix.markup_alt.meaning: Suffixes of the alternate prose-markup format that is rejected beneath the documentation root in favour of the stack's markup kind.

suffix.placeholder.meaning: Name patterns of placeholder/documentation files (configuration samples) that carry example values and are treated as documentation, not as the artifact kind they imitate.

suffix.telemetry_signal.meaning: How a telemetry signal definition file is recognised (a mechanical pattern, or a statement that recognition is judged with non-exhaustive examples).

suffix.telemetry_test.meaning: Name pattern that marks a test file as a telemetry test by filename colocation (identification by colocation alone).

suffix.telemetry_test_colocation.meaning: The file-name pattern by which a colocated test file is identified as a telemetry test — a family-scoped subset of test files, not a whole file kind; referenced by telemetry-family rules to scope out headerless telemetry tests.

suffix.test.meaning: File-name patterns that make a file a test file by filename alone, regardless of test category (unit, acceptance, e2e or other) or language.

suffix.test_exclusion.meaning: Name patterns of test files excluded from implementation-file marker and traceability obligations because they bind acceptance URNs instead of a component URN marker; the owning checker classifies a file as excluded by pattern match, not by test-kind classification.

suffix.test_files.meaning: Undifferentiated name patterns that mark a file as a test file of any kind (used e.g. to exclude tests from a scan), without asserting which test kind each pattern identifies.

suffix.train.meaning: Suffix or name pattern of a train definition artifact.

tooling.appendix_readable_formats.meaning: The appendix formats the stack's agent tooling (its designated file-reading tool) consumes directly as multimodal input; read-before-plan rules scope their multimodal-reading preference exactly to this list.
bunValues: PNG, JPG, SVG, PDF, audio, video (read directly as multimodal input)

tooling.appendix_type_map.meaning: How a referenced appendix's concrete observable format/kind is classified into an analysis type (e.g. mockup, spreadsheet, document, diagram, audio, video) to select type-specific analysis; supplies the observer values for appendix-type activation facts.
bunValues: Observable kinds: png, jpg, svg, pdf, audio, video, spreadsheet, document, diagram; the observer classifies the referenced appendix by type (mockup, spreadsheet, document, diagram, audio, video) to select the type-specific analysis

tooling.author.meaning: The stack's artifact authoring tool: the command that generates plan-derived artifacts which are schema-valid by construction, outside any plan session.

tooling.authoring_writer.meaning: The command that deterministically authors one unit of a locked plan decomposition.

tooling.contract_authoring.meaning: The authoring flow or command that adds a contract identity to the registry.

tooling.decision_registry_generator.meaning: The helper command that regenerates the decision registry from the decision records, and its check-only mode that reports drift without writing.
bunValues: atdd-bun docs adr-register (rewrites the adr-register region); atdd-bun docs adr-register --check reports drift without writing

tooling.delegation_context.meaning: How the delegated collaboration context is recognized in the stack: presence of the collaboration toolchain's project or ANY of its delegation seats places work inside the delegation chain that collaboration rules govern. Any single marker suffices — a partial chain, including a lone driver, is governed — and command-managed seats are not a prerequisite (owner-directed manual seat operations stay governed); absence of every marker takes the work out of scope.
bunValues: an atdd-flow project or any operator/main/coordinator/driver seat (any one marker suffices; partial chains, a single driver and owner-directed manual seat operations remain governed)

tooling.docs_generator.meaning: The helper command that regenerates generated documentation views from the current plan.

tooling.docs_renderer.meaning: The stack's reference renderer for the documentation corpus, with which the corpus must render; it must detect unresolvable internal references strongly enough that the check can report them as validation failures.

tooling.foreign_test_harnesses.meaning: Import specifiers / package names of foreign harnesses — test frameworks bound to their own runner and transform pipeline.

tooling.in_scope_languages.meaning: The languages of every file a stack's convention checks treat as in scope — production source and test files alike — serving as the realization's language gate.
bunValues: typescript, javascript (applies to source and test files alike; no file-kind restriction)

tooling.plan_command.meaning: The command that starts a gated plan/decomposition session.

tooling.plan_orchestrator.meaning: The command that runs the plan session (propose/ratify/confirm) and invokes the authoring writer on confirm.

tooling.runtime_config.meaning: (path) The runtime's own configuration file — a stack-identification marker alongside the native lockfiles.

tooling.scan_languages.meaning: The languages whose code files repository-wide code checks scan, covering production and test code alike.

tooling.seat_commands.meaning: The collaboration toolchain's canonical commands for seat lifecycle and handover, through which project-main, coordinator and driver seats must be managed.
bunValues: spawn, bind, pi runtime launch, task lifecycle, handover

tooling.stack_signals.meaning: How a repository (or package) is recognised as belonging to this stack: file markers and API-usage markers a stack observer can detect.
bunValues: bun.lock, bun.lockb, bunfig.toml at the project root; or a file importing bun:sqlite / using Bun.sql

tooling.test_harness.meaning: The import specifier of the declared runner's built-in test harness — the module test files must import their test API from.

tooling.test_languages.meaning: The languages of the stack's test files, used to scope test-discipline activation; they need not equal the production-source languages even when the values coincide.

tooling.test_runtime_family.meaning: The runtime values a test header may declare: the execution family of the stack's test runner, deliberately wider than the source-side runtime vocabulary.
bunValues: bun, browser, isomorphic, typescript, ts, node, js, javascript, deno, vite, astro, preact

tooling.typecheck.checker_dependencies.meaning: (list) The typechecker (or equivalent native implementation) that satisfies the dependency requirement when declared in the project's production or development dependencies.
bunValues: typescript; a native preview such as tsgo (counted from dependencies or devDependencies)

tooling.typecheck.config.meaning: (pattern) The language's type-configuration file: what must exist for types to be configured, whose strictness (and base inheritance) the check judges, and which variants the checker reads.
bunValues: tsconfig.json (obligation); tsconfig*.json read at the scan root

tooling.typecheck.no_emit_commands.meaning: (list) Helper commands recognized as running a no-emit typecheck; any of them in any check-path step satisfies the wiring (HOW) requirement.
bunValues: tsc --noEmit, tsgo --noEmit, vue-tsc, svelte-check, astro check, tsc --build

tooling.typecheck.step_names.meaning: (list) Check-path step names recognized as the typecheck step regardless of the command they run.

tooling.workflow_cli.meaning: The installed CLI that owns the durable workflow coordination records (tasks, seats, checkpoints, handovers, threads); only it mutates them, and its help output is the command authority.
bunValues: atdd-flow (also `bunx atdd-flow` when project-local and not on PATH)

tooling.worktree_cleanup.meaning: The governed command that performs worktree and delivery-branch cleanup when a driver seat is retired, and how it is resolved — never from the retiring seat worktree's own potentially stale copy.
bunValues: `atdd-bun worktree finish --delete-branch`, resolved from the primary checkout's local node_modules/.bin, then the primary checkout's own source when it is the ATDD Bun package, then PATH — never the seat worktree's copy

urn.acceptance_id.meaning: The identifier pattern of one acceptance (not itself a URN) that every acceptance id in this stack must match, in whatever components and padding the stack's format uses.
bunValues: AC-{STEP}-{NNN}, where STEP is the step code and NNN is the zero-padded index

urn.artifact.meaning: Shape of the URNs of the artifacts that planned components handle (event, state, data and config artifacts), and how the resource segment used for component-name derivation is identified.
bunValues: Resource = substring of the artifact URN after the colon; for dotted URNs (e.g. aspect.resource) the source examples use the final segment as the resource.

urn.artifact_name.meaning: Shape of a logical artifact name: the separator between name segments and the separator marking a variant in the final segment — the grammar that logical-to-physical mapping rules split on.
bunValues: ':' separates name segments, '.' separates a variant from its aspect (scenario:fragment, sensory:gesture.raw)

urn.binding.a11y.meaning: The syntax by which a test file binds an accessibility test URN (extends the artifact param with a11y).
bunValues: the spec carries an `A11Y` test URN.

urn.binding.contract.meaning: How a contract declares its URN (the field or construct that carries it).

urn.binding.telemetry.meaning: The syntax by which a test file declares (binds itself to) the telemetry URNs it claims, of any shape within the telemetry URN space.
bunValues: `// Telemetry:` header comment(s) listing the claimed telemetry URNs (e.g. `// Telemetry: telemetry:event:...`)

urn.binding.telemetry_item.meaning: The syntax by which a telemetry test file binds itself to a tracking-plan item (header comment, decorator, annotation), so that only tests bound this way count as the item's tests.
bunValues: tests bind to a tracking-plan item via a Telemetry: header in the test file

urn.binding.test.meaning: The syntax by which a test file declares its test URN in its leading comment block.
bunValues: // URN: test:{wagon}:{feature}:{ACCEPTANCE-ID} in the leading comment block

urn.builder.component.meaning: The stack's single canonical utility that constructs a component URN, with its call signature; convention cores that require builder-mediated URN construction refer to it instead of naming a utility.

urn.builder.wagon.meaning: The stack's designated construct (e.g. a builder method) by which code constructs a wagon URN; wagon URNs constructed in code or generated artifacts must be produced through it rather than hand-assembled strings.

urn.case_binding.acceptance.meaning: The syntax by which a single test case inside a test file binds itself to one or more acceptances (a per-case tag attached to the case), as distinct from the file-level binding.
bunValues: `// @covers` comment block directly above an it()/test() call, possibly several URNs on one line, binding one CASE rather than the file

urn.commit_receipt.meaning: The URN of the Acceptance Authority's commit receipt that a delivery train's terminal contract terminates in; used to derive family = delivery.

urn.contract.meaning: The URN shape by which an artifact declaration references a registered contract (as opposed to an artifact's own URN).
bunValues: theme[:seg...]:aspect.variant -- segments separated by ':', final segment after '.' (e.g. theme:seg1:seg2:aspect.variant or theme:aspect.variant)

urn.contract_id.meaning: The versioned contract id shape in the contract registry; a version-free contract URN maps to any version of the matching id.
bunValues: {domain}:{resource}[.{category}]:v{version}; urn contract:{domain}:{resource}[.{category}] maps to any version of id {domain}:{resource}[.{category}]:v*

urn.contract_registry_id.meaning: The id shape of a registered contract entry, and how a contract-reference URN maps to it (any version matches).
bunValues: URN contract:<domain>:<name> matches registry id <domain>:<name>:v<N> for any version N

urn.coverage_list.meaning: The construct by which a covering plan artifact (a feature) lists the plan artifacts it covers (its WMBTs); a coverage check matches each covered artifact against these lists.

urn.doc_id_declaration.meaning: The syntax by which an authored document declares its own document identifier.

urn.e2e_kinds.meaning: The test URN kinds a journey-bound spec may carry to satisfy an end-to-end browser-coverage obligation.

urn.e2e_test.meaning: Test-identity URN shape by which a canonical e2e test identifies itself — the feature and acceptance it proves.

urn.embedded_acceptance_identity.meaning: Where an acceptance embedded in a plan artifact declares its acceptance URN (the field path within the embedded acceptance object).
bunValues: identity.urn (the embedded acceptance object's identity: { urn: ... } field)

urn.exchanged_artifact.meaning: URN/naming pattern that an exchanged artifact (material, contract, schema) must follow, including its hierarchy/variant separator semantics — the concrete value of the 'naming-patterned' property of the artifact definition.
bunValues: theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant (colon for hierarchy, dot for variant)

urn.external_dependency.meaning: The reference shape, inside a plan artifact's component dependency list, that counts as an external dependency (as opposed to a component of another feature).

urn.harness_code_map.meaning: The stack's authoritative harness vocabulary: every valid harness name mapped to its exact, case-sensitive code that acceptance URNs embed and criteria templates share.
bunValues: unit->UNIT, http->HTTP, event->EVENT, ws->WS, e2e->E2E, a11y->A11Y, visual->VIS, metric->METRIC, job->JOB, db->DB, sec->SEC, load->LOAD, script->SCRIPT, widget->WIDGET, golden->GOLDEN, bloc->BLOC, integration->INTEGRATION, rls->RLS, edge_function->EDGE, realtime->REALTIME, storage->STORAGE, smoke->SMOKE

urn.header_fields.meaning: The syntax of a checked file's traceability header fields — identity URN, Tested-By, Runtime, Purpose — by which an observer recognizes which fields are present and on which lines.
bunValues: the URN, Tested-By, Runtime and Purpose header fields, found by a content scan for those field names

urn.hierarchy_separator.meaning: The character that separates hierarchy levels in artifact names (URNs).
bunValues: delegated to the sibling separator-semantics convention: 'hierarchy levels are counted using the hierarchy separator defined by the separator-semantics convention'

urn.identity_keys.meaning: The identity keys (field names) by which a plan artifact declares its identity; their declared values must be unique across scanned plan artifacts.
bunValues: train_id, interlocking_id, journey_id, urn, and other identity keys

urn.interface_artifact.meaning: Name shape of an artifact declared inside a plan artifact's produce/consume interface: a namespace segment (the owning domain), then the artifact name; a dotted sub-path may follow.

urn.interface_entry.meaning: The entry shapes by which a plan artifact's interface declares produced and consumed artifacts: name plus visibility on the produce side, name plus source on the consume side, including the source vocabulary.
bunValues: produce: array of {name: 'domain:artifact-name', to: 'internal|external'}; consume: array of {name: 'domain:artifact-name', from: 'wagon:slug|system:external|internal'}

urn.interlocking.meaning: URN shape of the interlocking artifact: the typed reference prefix by which a plan artifact references an interlocking.

urn.journey_markers.meaning: The stack's full set of header-comment journey markers by which any test file is recognized (judged) as a browser spec, including misnamed files; a superset of urn.binding.journey used for recognition only — an alternative marker alone does not provide the binding required for coverage.
bunValues: // Train:, // Journey:, // URN: test:train:…, // URN: test:journey:…

urn.journey_smoke_test.meaning: Test-identity URN shape of a browser-level smoke test whose subject is a journey.

urn.legacy_id.acceptance.meaning: The field or syntax by which an acceptance declares its legacy (backward-compatibility) id, parallel to the acceptance URN.

urn.name_carriers.meaning: The artifact kinds, locations and identity fields that carry an artifact name (names, URNs, schema identity fields), which a name change or migration must realign together.
bunValues: wagon manifest, feature file, URN, contract file location and $id field

urn.participant.meaning: The grammar of participant ids in a workflow (train) definition: the typed prefix per participant type (processing component, human actor, external system or data source) and the id-part syntax, including the combined validation pattern.
bunValues: wagon -> wagon:{wagon-id} (performs processing); user -> user:{role} (human actor); system -> system:{source} (external system/data source); validation pattern ^(wagon|user|system):[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$

urn.parts.acceptance.meaning: Named parts of the acceptance URN and their per-part constraints beyond the shape pattern (each part's form and the per-harness sequence range).
bunValues: Parts: wagon = kebab-case wagon; wmbt_id = step code + seq (C004); harness = UPPERCASE harness code; NNN = per-harness 001-999; slug = optional kebab descriptor.

urn.plan_identity_fields.meaning: For each recognized plan-artifact kind not identified by its own URN, the name of the field in which the artifact declares its canonical identity (its value is what other plan artifacts reference). Kinds that declare a URN are covered by the existing urn.declaration key, so this key deliberately excludes them.
bunValues: train -> train_id, interlocking -> interlocking_id, journey -> journey_id (the `urn` field for URN-identified kinds stays with urn.declaration)

urn.reference.journey.meaning: The marker by which a test file references a journey URN without binding to it, including the position (same as the stack's binding syntax, e.g. the header comment block) at which it is read; such a reference brings the file into journey-binding scope without satisfying the binding obligation.
bunValues: `// URN: test:journey:` — a header comment marker in the file's header block, the same position as the binding lines

urn.reference.train.meaning: The marker by which a test file references a train URN without binding to it, including the position (same as the stack's binding syntax, e.g. the header comment block) at which it is read; such a reference brings the file into journey-binding scope without satisfying the binding obligation.
bunValues: `// URN: test:train:` — a header comment marker in the file's header block, the same position as the binding lines

urn.responsive_test.meaning: The test URN a journey's responsive (browser) spec must carry in its header; this rule pins no further shape for it.
bunValues: RESP test URN (bun.json requires only "carrying a RESP test URN"; it prescribes no shape)

urn.telemetry.meaning: URN shape of a logical telemetry artifact.
bunValues: any concrete `telemetry:` URN — the `telemetry:`-prefixed URN space generally (e.g. `telemetry:event:be:example:item-accepted`); claimed URNs and headerless assertions are not limited to the event form

urn.telemetry_item.meaning: The identifier of one telemetry item in the tracking plan, so a checker can match acceptance-required items, plan entries and test bindings by exact identifier. It is an identifier contract, not a restrictive grammar: every telemetry URN the tracking plan declares is covered.

urn.telemetry_kinds.meaning: URN kind segments by which a test identifies itself as a telemetry test.

urn.telemetry_test_kind_segments.meaning: The kind segments of a test's own identifier (URN) that mark the test as a telemetry test; referenced by telemetry-family rules to identify headerless telemetry tests and scope them out of the binding check.

urn.test.meaning: URN shape of a test file and the classification codes it may carry (here: the code that marks a test as responsive).
bunValues: a test URN (e.g. `test:train:…`, `test:journey:…`) may carry harness codes; the responsive code is `RESP`
test URN carrying dash-delimited kind segments (`-INPUT-`, `-VALIDATION-`, `-VALIDATE-`); bun.json states the segment form only, not the full URN shape

urn.theme_map.meaning: Path of the canonical theme map: the registry that declares the themes a theme-first artifact/contract identity may start with

urn.train_e2e_test.meaning: Test-identity URN shape of a browser-level e2e test whose subject is a train (the route's train).

urn.train_sequence_artifact.meaning: The reference form for the plan artifacts listed in a train's sequence: a short domain-and-resource reference, distinct from the referenced artifact's full URN.

urn.variant_separator.meaning: The character that separates variant levels in artifact names (URNs).
bunValues: the dot: 'Variant levels are counted as dots'
